01 / The starting point

Overview

A direct-to-consumer snack box company I founded, with $20K+ in sales and a 57% returning customer rate.

02 / The why

Problem

Trying a new snack often means committing to a full-size box of one thing. I built SnackSpot for shoppers who wanted a mix of snacks without that commitment.

03 / The thinking

Approach

I founded and ran the company end to end, built the e-commerce storefront, and set the SEO strategy to bring in customers through search. I developed six boxes for different customers and occasions: Classic, Canadian, Office, Student, Gluten-Free, and Wellness. The Canadian box responded to interest in supporting locally made products. The Office box served company orders around holidays and large events. When offices asked to add their own logos or stickers, I made the boxes customizable. Boxes contained 25 to 50 items, priced from $29.99 to $44.99 CAD.

04 / The takeaways

Outcome

SnackSpot generated $20K+ in sales since the e-commerce site opened, with a 57% returning customer rate. The Office box accounted for over 75% of site orders. Customer requests showed me how customization could turn a standard product into one that fits a group. Office orders followed holidays and events, so I learned to think about demand by occasion, not just by customer. If I restarted, I would launch with office kits first, keep the variety inside each box, and begin outreach with local offices. I would also explore seasonal bundles with custom logos and volume pricing to make larger orders and yearly reorders easier.
